artwork.prompt: Edit the first photograph into one exactly square (1:1) full-bleed documentary close-up for The Vegetable Guru crop-rotation page. Keep its crumbly dark brown garden soil, subdued natural colour, slightly oblique overhead angle and softly diffused Cornish daylight. Replace the pair with a single loose bunch of four or five freshly lifted orange carrots set down together on the earth. Use the carrots on the left of reference 2 to guide the overlapping pose and unequal shapes, and the actual orange roots in reference 3 for believable homegrown skin and shape. Roots and attached fine green carrot fronds only. Closely grouped, untied and casually tilted on one diagonal. A short, blunt root sits forward off-axis with a long slender taper partly tucked beneath a broad, faintly crooked shoulder. One smaller root is partly obscured. Let neighbouring crowns touch at different heights, stems drape unevenly, and tips point at noticeably different angles. A few patches of caught soil near crowns and natural roots. Use real contact shadows, a warm but believable carrot orange and enough light to read when printed at 24 mm. Orange roots dominate the square, most root tips stay in frame, and a little foliage can run off the upper edge. Keep enough surrounding soil to make the bunch legible at a glance. Show only this bunch and soil. No kale, beetroot, person, hands, twine, props, words, borders, studio lighting, symmetrical fan, evenly spaced carrots, glossy supermarket polish or illustration.
